quran.note: Hud, the brother of ʿAad, calls them to worship Allah alone; the chiefs call him foolish and ask him to bring what he promises; Hud and those with him are saved.
The same call; “you have not brought us clear evidence”; the people of Hud are destroyed.
Hud warns ‘Aad, asks no payment, and reminds them of Allah’s favours.
Warning in al-Ahqaf; the cloud they took for rain was a wind with a painful punishment, and nothing was seen of them but their dwellings.
A violent wind for seven nights and eight days; “do you see any remains?”

hadith.summary: The Prophet ﷺ said he was given victory by the Saba wind (the easterly) and that the people of ‘Ad were destroyed by the Dabur wind (the westerly).

Aisha said she never saw the Prophet ﷺ laugh fully, only smile, and that when he saw a cloud or a strong wind it showed on his face. Asked why, he said he could not be sure it did not carry a punishment, since a people had been punished by a wind, and when they saw the punishment they said it was a cloud bringing rain.
hadith.note: The report does not name ‘Ad; it is placed in the Sahih under the commentary on Qur’an 46:24, which tells of the cloud that ‘Ad took for rain.

scholarly.work: Tafsir Ibn Kathir (abridged English edition, read on Quran.com)
scholarly.author: Ibn Kathir
scholarly.summary: Calls Hud “the brother of ‘Ad”, sent to the first people of ‘Ad, who lived in al-Ahqaf. It says the cloud they took for rain was a wind that destroyed everything it could by Allah’s command, and that nothing could be seen but their dwellings. It cites, without grades, a report in Ibn Majah through Ibn Abbas (“May Allah have mercy on us and on the brother of ‘Ad”) and reports of Aisha in Ahmad, al-Bukhari and Muslim on the Prophet’s ﷺ unease at clouds and wind.
